newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin Energy, Northern States end merger.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin Energy, Northern States end merger.

text.p: Wisconsin Energy Co. and Northern States Power Co. said Friday they terminated their plans to combine into one power company, two days after federal energy regulators rejected the planned $6 billion merger.
But the companies said they have agreed to examine several potential collaborative efforts that came up during the merger planning process.
The merger would have combined the companies into Primergy Corp.
"Continuing the Primergy transaction, given the current regulatory climate, is not in the best interests of our stockholders, customers and employees," Wisconsin Energy Chairman Richard Abdoo said.

He said there were many factors in reaching the decision including the action by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Wednesday and expected delays or changes that would reduce the benefits of the planned merger.
Officials of both companies have agreed to examine potential collaborations identified during the merger planning process.

The companies announced their merger plan on May 1, 1995. The decision to end the merger was approved by both companies' boards and NSP and Wisconsin Energy will withdraw the merger applications from state and federal agencies.
